items.title: 68091_Joe Turner oral history interview
items.q: So we had LaVerne La Baker, had The Drifters, the Fives (?). We had a bunch of 'em...blues singers. So we all took off to Australia...

ctx.x: So we...we started...we started recording that. After that, we made "Corrine Corrina," "Sweet Sixteen," "Honey Hush." 'N' lemme see...so many a numbers we made. "Chained Love." We made a whole lot of numbers, so I was the hottest thing out on the block. Ruth Brown was workin' for Atlantic Recording Company. She had...she had a number out, "Mama, You Treat Your Daughter Mean." So I got acquainted with her, an' we went on rock 'n' roll shows. We'd get...fourteen or twenty acts and go down South and play rock 'n'…

I never had met him, so, finally, I met him in New York City. Him and his band. So he took me out, and we had dinner, an' we had us a ball. So he said he was goin' to take me on some o' his shows wit' him. So we had LaVerne La Baker, had The Drifters, the Fives (?). We had a bunch of 'em...blues singers. So we all took off to Australia... went to Australia. I left here. We come to California, and then we left and went to Australia. So I come here to see my mother, and then I... I promised I was gonna buy her a…

This house I'm in right now, I bought it for my mother. We looked all over California. Had some fellow out there, lived across the street from where I did. He was real estate man so he took me to ride around to a lot of old places I didn't like. I say, "I don't put my mother in no place like this."
